title: A deposit's manifest, schema version 1.0
description: The document at the root of a deposit that says which files the deposit consists of. docs/spec/deposit-layout.md is the prose this is the normative form of, and docs/decisions/layout.md is why the schema and not the prose decides what is refused. What this schema judges is the manifest as a document: its keys, the shape of an entry, the form of a path and of a digest. What it cannot judge is everything that requires opening another file, because a schema sees one document and a manifest is a claim about a directory; those are listed in deferred_checks and are why a manifest that validates here is not yet a manifest that matches its deposit.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema the manifest is written against. A string rather than a number, for the reason docs/decisions/schema-language.md gives: 1.10 and 1.1 are one JSON number and two schema versions.

file_count.description: The number of files listed. docs/decisions/dataset-unit.md requires it beside the per-file checksums. It catches a files array that lost entries to something that was not parsing the document, and it is not a defence against anybody who edited the manifest, who could decrement it.

files.description: One entry per file in the deposit, except manifest.json itself, which cannot carry its own digest. A deposit with no files is not a deposit.

entry.description: What one file is claimed to be: where it sits, how long it is, what its bytes hash to, and which of the three kinds of file it is.

size.description: The length of the file in bytes. Compared before the digest, because it is cheap where a digest is a full read and because truncation is what a size mismatch usually is.

role.description: What kind of file this is, which is what a reader dispatches on. Coarse on purpose and not the role an array plays in the measurement, which comes from the metadata document: the manifest asks what kind of file this is, the metadata asks what this array is.

path.description: Where the file sits, relative to the deposit root, with / as the separator. The character set is narrower than any filesystem requires so that a deposit written on one system and read on another arrives intact. No . or .. component, because a reader that resolved ../ out of a deposit is a reader an untrusted deposit can steer, and this format is read on machines belonging to people who did not write the deposit. Not manifest.json, because a document cannot carry the digest of the bytes that carry the digest.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes, all of them, lowercase hexadecimal with the algorithm in front of it. docs/decisions/identity.md decides the algorithm and the prefix; the prefix is what lets a second algorithm arrive later without any stored digest becoming ambiguous about which one produced it.

deferred_checks.refusal: file_count and the length of files disagree.

deferred_checks.cannot: compares an entry against every other entry
deferred_checks.refusal: a path is listed more than once, so two entries claim one file.

deferred_checks.cannot: reads a file outside the document
deferred_checks.refusal: a file the manifest lists is not in the deposit.

deferred_checks.cannot: reads a file outside the document
deferred_checks.refusal: a file is a different length from its entry, which is what a truncated transfer looks like.

deferred_checks.cannot: reads a file outside the document
deferred_checks.refusal: a file's bytes do not hash to its entry's digest.

deferred_checks.cannot: reads the directory the document sits in
deferred_checks.refusal: a file in the deposit is named by no entry, so the deposit on disk and the deposit in the manifest are different objects.

deferred_checks.cannot: reads the bytes of the document rather than its values
deferred_checks.refusal: the manifest's encoding is not the one a transfer must not have changed.
